summary: Managed servers now keep ownership of their detached process group after the direct launcher exits. Stop, restart, switch, startup timeout, and controller shutdown wait until the group contains no live processes before clearing the PID and releasing server capacity.

Finite verification uses the same ownership mechanism. Cancellation, timeout, launcher exit, and shutdown remain non-terminal until stubborn descendants have exited, including descendants that close inherited output streams.
A failed cleanup preserves the owned PID, capacity slot, active test slot, and worktree exclusion so an operator can retry without reporting a false stopped or terminal state.
